questions.question: A series of paintings illustrating the verses of ‘Vande Mataram’ and published in the ‘Bande Mataram Album’ were displayed as view-cutters along Kartavya Path during Republic Day Parade 2026. Who was the painter, and in which year were they created?
questions.questionHtml: A series of paintings illustrating the verses of ‘Vande Mataram’ and published in the ‘Bande Mataram Album’ were displayed as view-cutters along Kartavya Path during Republic Day Parade 2026. Who was the painter, and in which year were they created?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tejendra Kumar Mitra, 1923.

In News

  • A series of paintings illustrating the verses of the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ were displayed as view-cutters along Kartavya Path during the Republic Day Parade 2026.

Key Points

  • The paintings displayed were created by Shri Tejendra Kumar Mitra in the year 1923.
  • These artworks were originally published in the ‘Bande Mataram Album’ (1923) and were selected to align with the parade's theme of "150 years of Vande Mataram".
  • The display was intended to visually illustrate the verses of the national song for the spectators at Kartavya Path.
  • This initiative was part of the broader cultural showcase which also included pan-India band performances and floral decorations themed around Vande Mataram.

Additional Information

  • Theme Context
    • The 2026 Republic Day was celebrated with the central theme of 150 years of Vande Mataram.
    • Videos on Vande Mataram were played on screens at Kartavya Path to complement the static displays.
  • Related Performances
    • Performance venues for the Vande Mataram theme included the ancestral home of Rishi Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay at Kanthalpara, Naihati.
    • A banner depicting ‘Vande Mataram’ was unveiled along with the release of rubber balloons at the conclusion of the parade.
  • Tableaux
    • Tableaux were presented under the themes “Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram” and “Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat”.

questions.question: What were the two broader themes on which the tableaux were presented during the Republic Day Parade 2026?

options.text: "Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat" and "Nari Shakti under Viksit Bharat"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram" and "Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat".

In News

  • The Tableaux during the Republic Day Parade 2026 were presented under the broader themes of “Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram” and “Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat”.

Key Points

  • The two specific themes chosen for the Tableaux were “Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram” (Mantra of Freedom – Vande Mataram) and “Samriddhi ka Mantra – Atmanirbhar Bharat” (Mantra of Prosperity – Self-Reliant India).
  • A total of 30 Tableaux (17 from States/UTs and 13 from Ministries/Departments/Services) were selected to roll down Kartavya Path reflecting these themes.
  • States like Chhattisgarh and Gujarat explicitly focused on the "Swatantrata ka Mantra – Vande Mataram" theme, while others like Tamil Nadu and Kerala highlighted self-reliance and prosperity.
  • The cultural performances by approximately 2,500 artists were also organized under these same two broader themes.

Additional Information

  • Specific State Themes
    • Assam's tableau was themed "Ashirakandi: The craft village".
    • Uttar Pradesh showcased the "Culture of Bundelkhand".
    • Jammu & Kashmir presented "Handicrafts and Folk Dances of Jammu and Kashmir".
  • Ministry Themes
    • The Ministry of Culture's tableau was titled "Vande Mataram: The Soul-Cry of a Nation".
    • The Indian Navy's theme was "Samudra Se Samridhi".
  • Overall Parade Theme
    • The broader context for the entire parade was established as "150 years of Vande Mataram".

questions.question: Project Veer Gatha, aimed at inspiring children about the gallant deeds of the Armed Forces, was jointly initiated by which two Union Ministries?
questions.questionHtml: Project Veer Gatha, aimed at inspiring children about the gallant deeds of the Armed Forces, was jointly initiated by which two Union Ministries?

options.text: Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Education
options.html: Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Education

options.text: Ministry of Education and Ministry of Defence
options.html: Ministry of Education and Ministry of Defence

options.text: Ministry of Culture and Ministry of Defence
options.html: Ministry of Culture and Ministry of Defence

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and Ministry of Defence
options.html: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and Ministry of Defence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Education and Ministry of Defence.

In News

  • Project Veer Gatha 5.0 was jointly organised by the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Defence as part of Republic Day celebrations.

Key Points

  • Project Veer Gatha 5.0 was conducted from 08 September 2025 to 10 November 2025.
  • The initiative was jointly undertaken by the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Defence.
  • It aimed to inspire school children about the bravery and sacrifices of India’s Armed Forces.
  • Approximately 1.92 crore school students participated across India.

Additional Information

  • Project Veer Gatha is a nationwide initiative to inculcate values of patriotism and courage among students.
  • Ministry of Education oversees school education and student engagement programmes in India.
  • Ministry of Defence plays a key role in preserving and promoting the legacy of the Armed Forces.
  • Selected student winners of Veer Gatha 5.0 were felicitated in New Delhi and attended the Republic Day Parade.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26 tabled in Parliament, what are the projected growth rates for real GDP and Gross Value Added (GVA) for Financial Year 2026, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26 tabled in Parliament, what are the projected growth rates for real GDP and Gross Value Added (GVA) for Financial Year 2026, respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7.4 per cent and 7.3 per cent.

In News

  • Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman tabled the Economic Survey 2025-26 in Parliament, highlighting India's economic performance.

Key Points

  • According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the First Advance Estimates place FY26 real GDP growth at 7.4 per cent.
  • The Gross Value Added (GVA) growth for FY26 is estimated at 7.3 per cent.
  • These figures reaffirm India’s status as the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year, despite a fragile global environment.
  • Private Final Consumption Expenditure grew by 7.0 per cent in FY26, reaching 61.5 per cent of GDP.

Additional Information

  • Investment Activity (FY26)
    • Gross Fixed Capital Formation: Grew by 7.8 per cent.
    • Share in GDP: Remained steady at 30 per cent.
  • Services Sector
    • Services remain the main driver of growth.
    • Estimated growth for the entire fiscal year is 9.1 per cent.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book “Sing, Dance and Lead: Leadership Lessons from the Life of Srila Prabhupada”, launched by the Vice-President of India?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of the book “Sing, Dance and Lead: Leadership Lessons from the Life of Srila Prabhupada”, launched by the Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hindol Sengupta.

In News

  • Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the book “Sing, Dance and Lead: Leadership Lessons from the Life of Srila Prabhupada” authored by Hindol Sengupta.

Key Points

  • The book is written by Hindol Sengupta, a noted author and commentator.
  • It draws leadership lessons from the life and teachings of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.
  • The book presents leadership as ethical, service-oriented and value-driven.
  • Theme of the Book
    • Leadership through inspiration rather than authority
    • Joyful, participative and human-centred leadership
    • Enduring impact through institution-building

Additional Information

  • Srila Prabhupada
    • Founder of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON)
    • Established ISKCON in 1966
    • Known for spreading Indian spiritual philosophy globally
  • Launch Event
    • Held at the Vice-President’s Enclave, New Delhi
    • Attended by Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
    • Included senior ISKCON and Akshaya Patra Foundation leaders
  • Significance
    • Links Indian civilisational values with modern leadership thought
    • Highlights ethics, humility and service in public life
    • Aims to inspire youth towards transformational leadership

questions.question: Which eco-sensitive zone did the National Green Tribunal issue a notice on non-compliance of environmental norms in January 2026?
questions.questionHtml: Which eco-sensitive zone did the National Green Tribunal issue a notice on non-compliance of environmental norms in January 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Taj Trapezium Zone.

In News

  • The National Green Tribunal (NGT) issued a notice to the Union Government and the Uttar Pradesh government over non-compliance with environmental norms in the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ).

Key Points

  • TTZ is an eco-sensitive area of about 10,400 sq. km, created to protect the Taj Mahal from pollution and ecological degradation.
  • It covers Agra region and includes heritage sites like Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
  • The TTZ regime was established based on Supreme Court directions in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996) to enforce strict pollution control measures.
  • Tree felling within 5 km of the Taj Mahal requires prior permission, as per Supreme Court directions in M.C. Mehta (2015).

Additional Information

  • National Green Tribunal (NGT)
    • Established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
    • Ensures speedy and effective disposal of cases related to environmental protection and conservation.
  • Key Environmental Laws under NGT
    • Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
    • Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
    • Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
  • Supreme Court Orders
    • M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996): Directed strong pollution-control measures in TTZ.
    • M.C. Mehta (2015): Restricted tree felling within 5 km of Taj Mahal.
  • Other Eco-Sensitive Zones in India
    • Sundarbans Reserve Zone: Mangrove region in West Bengal.
    • Western Ghats Eco-Sensitive Zone: Mountain range with high biodiversity across multiple states.
    • Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve: Protected area across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.
